Hi Alina,
Indeed, Renjin can't run caret due to problems building/running it's dependencies.

I took a quick look at one of the blockers, the foreach package, and updated Renjin with a quick fix, so now that at least is resolved.

The only remaining blocker for caret is then (ultimately) Matrix, which is failing due to some remaining problems with Renjin's S4 implementation:

" methods can add arguments to the generic 'toeplitz' only if '...' is an argument to the generic"
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/Matrix/1.2-3/build/13

This is something we're actively working on, but one way to help is to help reduce these kinds of errors down to simple test cases.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Usage of gcc-bridge on dependent libraries
messages.subject_clean: Usage of gcc-bridge on dependent libraries
messages.body_plain:
Hi Christian!

Let me walk you through this a bit as this hasn't properly been documented yet.

1) Namespaces and Linking

First, it's helpful to walk through how different sources / libraries get compiled together in GCC/Native land.

Each source file is compiled independently. If you compile a Fortran source file from the BLAS library that uses the LSAME function, for example, it will simply generate an object file that references the unresolved symbol lsame_.  (Fortran function names are mangled <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_mangling#Fortran> with a trailing underscore)

$ gcc -c dgemm.f
$ nm dgemm.o
0000000000000000 T dgemm_
                 U lsame_
$ gcc -c lsame.f
$ nm lsame.o
0000000000000000 T lsame_

After compiling all the individual source files from a library, you normally archive the resulting objects files into a single object file like libblas.a, for example. This is not much different than a jar file.

When you finally compile a shared library or an executable that relies on libblas, then GCC will actually perform the linking, mapping references in mlapack to dgemm, for example, to the symbol defined in libblas.a. Note that there is no namespacing here, it's all just a sea of flat symbol names. If you defined your own dgemm_ function in mplapack, that symbol would be used instead of the one defined in libblas.a.

GCC-Bridge follows an analogous procedure. The compilation phase is largely the same, but we enable our plugin which dumps out the gimple for each source file:

$ gcc -c -m32 -fplugin=/path/to/bridge.so dgemm.f

This creates a dgemm.gimple file alongside the dgemm.o file. The two files contain largely the same information - just that Gimple is a much higher-level representation of the functions defined in dgemm.f than the x86 machine code in dgemm.o.

The real work for us starts when the GCC Bridge GimpleCompiler runs, collects all the .gimple files, and compiles each function in the gimple to a JVM static method.

JVM object code is of course organized differently, not into a table of symbols but into class files and their methods. Arbitrarily, GCC Bridge, generates one JVM class per source file, and a public
static method in that class for every function:

$ javap scabs1.class
Compiled from "scabs1.f"
public class org.renjin.math.scabs1 {
  public static float scabs1_(float[], int);
}

The package here ("org.renjin.math") is also arbitrary and provided as option to GCC-Bridge.

GCC-Bridge is also performing a link-step during compilation. Just like the GNU Linker, it maps symbolic names to the location of the compile code. In the native case, the linking is done from name to an offset in the object file. In our case, we link the symbol name to a JVM class and method name.

So the short answer to your question is that yes, nothing should stop you from dumping all the sources files of mplapack and its dependencies into a single directory and compiling with GCC-Bridge.

2) Depending on GCC-Bridge Compiled Libraries

Of course, with GCC-Bridge we wanted to be able to link together libraries compiled separately in a manner that's at least analogous to how linking works in GCC-land. For this reason, GCC-Bridge also emits metadata for each compiled function.  If you open renjin-blas <https://nexus.bedatadriven.com/service/local/repo_groups/public/content/org/renjin/renjin-blas/0.8.2087/renjin-blas-0.8.2087.jar>.jar from nexus.bedatadriven.com <http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/>, you'll find a set of text files in META-INF/org.renjin.gcc.symbols that help GCC-Bridge map the raw symbol names (like 'dgemv_' for fortran) to the previously-compiled Java methods.

For example:
META-INF/org.renjin.gcc.symbols/dgemv_

Contains the  properties file:
type=METHOD
class=org/renjin/math/dgemv__
member=dgemv_
descriptor=(Lorg/renjin/gcc/runtime/BytePtr;...I)V

This means that you add compiled libraries just like any other Maven dependency:

<dependency>
  <groupId>org.renjin</groupId>
  <artifactId>renjin-blas</artifactId>
  <version>0.8.2087</version>
</dependency>

And then when you compile-link the mplapack sources with GCC-Bridge, it will use this metadata to find the compiled JVM method provided by renjin-blas.jar

I haven't set up an lapack build yet, but will need to do sometime in the near future as there are a few R packages with native code that link directly to LAPACK. I can help you set it up in the Renjin parallel to the math/blas module.

3) GCC-Bridge compiler errors

It looks like the CEIL_DIV_EXPR is an operation that we haven't encountered for and for which GCC-Bridge doesn't know how to generate bytecode. From the GCC Docs <https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gccint/Unary-and-Binary-Expressions.html>, it looks like it's an integer division, rounded towards positive infinity.  You can add this to GimpleOp.java, and then add the code generation logic to ExprFactory.java.

However, it looks like this particular error is generated from one of the blas/zxxxx sources, which are routines for complex numbers, which you may not need. (Hopefully not - I think there are a still a number of issues in addition to the one above affecting BLAS complex number routines).

If you set up a fork of mplapack on GitHub I'd be happy to help you through issues that you encounter.

Best,
Alex

> > >
> > > Normally, ScriptEngines allow you to specify the stdout/stderr streams via the ScriptEngine API like the following:
> > >
> > > ScriptEngineManager scriptEngineManager = new ScriptEngineManager();
> > > ScriptEngine scriptEngine = scriptEngineManager.getEngineByName("foobar");
> > >
> > > scriptEngine.getContext().setWriter(writer);
> > > scriptEngine.getContext().setErrorWriter(writer);
> > >
> > > scriptEngine.eval( ... );
> > >
> > > After, this the evaluated script emits the output to the writer specified. Unfortunately, this does not seem to be the case for Renjin. It ignores the the standard settings and emits output to the standard output and error.
> > >
> > > I have put together a test, which demonstrates the issue, in contrast to JavaScript ScriptEngine (Java 8 built-in / Nashorn), which correctly performs the redirection:
> > >
> > > import org.testng.Assert;
> > > import org.testng.annotations.Test;
> > >
> > > import javax.script.ScriptEngine;
> > > import javax.script.ScriptEngineManager;
> > > import javax.script.ScriptException;
> > > import java.io.StringWriter;
> > > import java.io.Writer;

> > > public class RenjinTest {
> > >
> > >
> > >     @Test
> > >     public void testJavaScriptScriptEngine() throws ScriptException {
> > >
> > >         testScriptEngine("JavaScript", "print('Hello World')");
> > >     }
> > >
> > >
> > >     @Test
> > >     public void testRenjinScriptScriptEngine() throws ScriptException {
> > >
> > >         testScriptEngine("Renjin", "cat('Hello World')");
> > >     }
> > >
> > >     private void testScriptEngine(String scriptEngineName, String helloWorldScript) throws ScriptException {
> > >
> > >         StringWriter stringWriter = new StringWriter();
> > >
> > >         ScriptEngineManager scriptEngineManager = new ScriptEngineManager();
> > >         ScriptEngine scriptEngine = scriptEngineManager.getEngineByName(scriptEngineName);
> > >         if(scriptEngine == null) {
> > >             throw new IllegalStateException("Could not load ScriptEngine: " + scriptEngineName);
> > >         }
> > >
> > >         Writer originalWriter = scriptEngine.getContext().getWriter();
> > >         Writer errorWriter = scriptEngine.getContext().getErrorWriter();
> > >
> > >         try {
> > >
> > >             scriptEngine.getContext().setWriter(stringWriter);
> > >             scriptEngine.getContext().setErrorWriter(stringWriter);
> > >
> > >             scriptEngine.eval(helloWorldScript);
> > >
> > >         } finally {
> > >
> > >             scriptEngine.getContext().setWriter(originalWriter);
> > >             scriptEngine.getContext().setErrorWriter(errorWriter);
> > >         }
> > >
> > >         Assert.assertEquals(stringWriter.toString().trim(), "Hello World");
> > >     }
> > > }

> > >         <dependency>
> > >             <groupId>org.renjin</groupId>
> > >             <artifactId>renjin-script-engine</artifactId>
> > >             <version>0.8.2062</version>
> > >             <scope>compile</scope>
> > >         </dependency>
> > >         <dependency>
> > >             <groupId>org.testng</groupId>
> > >             <artifactId>testng</artifactId>
> > >             <version>6.8.21</version>
> > >             <scope>test</scope>
> > >         </dependency>
> > >
> > > After doing some research, I have found that technically one can work-around this issue by performing the following:
> > >
> > > PrintWriter printWriter = // ...
> > >
> > > ScriptEngine scriptEngine = // ...
> > >
> > > ((org.renjin.script.RenjinScriptEngine) scriptEngine).getSession().getConnectionTable().getStdout().setOutputStream(printWriter);
> > > ((org.renjin.script.RenjinScriptEngine) scriptEngine).getSession().getConnectionTable().getStderr().setOutputStream(printWriter);
> > >
> > > However, this means we loose all the benefits of having a non-implementation dependent ScriptEngine API. (Consider a generic tool, which can run multiple languages).

> > > Would it be possible to have this issue fixed in the code base? Do you by any change know how should I request/report this?

messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex!

Thank you very much for this detailed and quick response!!

>And then when you compile-link the mplapack sources with GCC-Bridge, it will use this metadata to find the compiled JVM method provided by renjin-blas.jar

Cool, the logic behind this plugin is awesome.

> And then when you compile-link the mplapack sources with GCC-Bridge, it will use this metadata to find the compiled JVM method provided by renjin-blas.jar
>
> I haven't set up an lapack build yet, but will need to do sometime in the near future as there are a few R packages with native code that link directly to LAPACK. I can help you set it up in the Renjin parallel to the math/blas module.
>
> 3) GCC-Bridge compiler errors
>
> It looks like the CEIL_DIV_EXPR is an operation that we haven't encountered for and for which GCC-Bridge doesn't know how to generate bytecode. From the GCC Docs <https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gccint/Unary-and-Binary-Expressions.html>, it looks like it's an integer division, rounded towards positive infinity.  You can add this to GimpleOp.java, and then add the code generation logic to ExprFactory.java.
>
>
> However, it looks like this particular error is generated from one of the blas/zxxxx sources, which are routines for complex numbers, which you may not need. (Hopefully not - I think there are a still a number of issues in addition to the one above affecting BLAS complex number routines).

Thanks for giving me the starting points. and yes you are right i do not need complex numbers.
so i have deleted all the lapack/src/main/fortran/z*.f files. I have also removed all the blas source code (and now just use renjin blas as maven dependency - that is really cool)

But i still keep getting the same build failure:

[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.renjin:gcc-bridge-maven-plugin:0.9.0-SNAPSHOT:compile (default) on project lapack: Exception compiling cgbrfsx.f. No enum constant org.renjin.gcc.gimple.GimpleOp.CEIL_DIV_EXPR (through reference chain: org.renjin.gcc.gimple.GimpleCompilationUnit["functions"]->org.renjin.gcc.gimple.GimpleFunction["basicBlocks"]->org.renjin.gcc.gimple.GimpleBasicBlock["statements"]->org.renjin.gcc.gimple.statement.GimpleAssignment["operator"]) -> [Help 1]

>
> If you set up a fork of mplapack on GitHub I'd be happy to help you through issues that you encounter.

I have started this github project for all topics of this thread -> https://github.com/KIC/gcc-bridged-mplapack and already pushed some sources to it. If you want to take a look you could also just use the provided Dockerfile. I have discovered two things

1.) mplapack's reqiurement for blas is of version 3.1.0
2.) but it is also optional (highly recommendend - whatever this means).

so i have downloaded the 3.1.0 blas source and used the renjin blas maven module as a starting point. So the plain blas build fails with some gimple_assign issue
 -> Exception compile to class files: Exception compiling function ctbsv [ctbsv_] in unit ctbsv.f.gimple: Exception compiling instruction gimple_assign<RDIV_EXPR, T1781, T1776, T1780>  #215: Exception compiling assignment to gimple_assign<RDIV_EXPR, T1781, T1776, T1780>  #215: op: RDIV_EXPR -> [Help 1]

 -> https://github.com/KIC/gcc-bridged-mplapack/issues/1

but! since the blas/lapack dependency is optional i have just copied all mplack sources to their desired folder (fortran,c,cpp) and started the build with gcc-bridge - it requires a lot of heap > 2G and fails with a NPE
 -> https://github.com/KIC/gcc-bridged-mplapack/issues/2

Thanks for your help!

Chris

PS to start from a clean basis you can use init.sh and pass the lapack version as argument. then just cd lapack; mvn clean install

messages.body_plain:
Hi Roosha,
It's hard to say without seeing how your project is set up.

One thing that might help diagnose the problem is to instantiate
RenjinScriptEngine directly rather than rely on the
ScriptEngineManager which, most unfortunately, swallows any exception
that occurs and just returns null.

Can you try creating the RenjinScriptEngine in the following way:

RenjinScriptEngine engine = new RenjinScriptEngineFactory().getScriptEngine();

Can you share any stack trace that you receive along with your pom.xml file ?

Best,
ALex

Hi Alexander

Actually adding this CEIL_DIV_EXPR in three classes was in fact not that a big deal (ok, could be that the result is not doing exactly what Opcodes.IDIV; does, but at least it should compile. Sadly I run now in the same NullPointer as I do in the mplapack.
Can you help me a little bit further on this? If you have docker installed you can simply do so:

wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KIC/gcc-bridged-mplapack/master/docker/Dockerfile
docker build -t gccbridged
docker run --rm -it gccbridged /bin/bash

root@42923319b074:~/gcc-bridged-mplapack# cd lapack/
root@42923319b074:~/gcc-bridged-mplapack/lapack# mvn clean install

which gives me

[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.renjin:gcc-bridge-maven-plugin:0.9.0-SNAPSHOT:compile (default) on project lapack: Exception compile to class files: Exception creating FunctionGenerator for xerbla_array in xerbla_array.f: Exception for parameter srname_array of type unsigned int8[][]*: NullPointerException -> [Help 1] [ERROR]

Thx and all the best
Christian

messages.body_plain:
Hi

My first successfully compiled c project is ecos https://github.com/KIC/gcc-bridged-mplapack/tree/master/ecos a convex/cone solver. Now I need again some help because I can not get the Java test case to compile / run.

The return type of record class is not recognized in my test source: https://github.com/KIC/gcc-bridged-mplapack/blob/master/ecos/src/test/java/ecos/RandomFeasible.java

// does not compile the class lookis like org.gccbridged.ecos.record$pwork0 but I can not cast ...
org.gccbridged.ecos.record.pwork0 pwork0 = ECOS.ECOS_setup(random_feasible_n, random_feasible_m, random_feasible_p, random_feasible_l, random_feasible_ncones, random_feasible_q, random_feasible_nexc,
        random_feasible_Gpr, random_feasible_Gjc, random_feasible_Gir,
        random_feasible_Apr, random_feasible_Ajc, random_feasible_Air,
        random_feasible_c, random_feasible_h, random_feasible_b);

I thought, well then I will just assign the result to an Object and try to inspect more at runtime and do some castings later. However the following code throws an Unsatisfied Link exception at runtime:
Object pwork0 = ECOS.ECOS_setup(random_feasible_n, random_feasible_m, random_feasible_p, random_feasible_l, random_feasible_ncones, random_feasible_q, random_feasible_nexc,
        random_feasible_Gpr, random_feasible_Gjc, random_feasible_Gir,
        random_feasible_Apr, random_feasible_Ajc, random_feasible_Air,
        random_feasible_c, random_feasible_h, random_feasible_b);

org.renjin.gcc.runtime.UnsatisfiedLinkException: Function 'clock_gettime' was not found at compile-time

    at org.gccbridged.ecos.timer__.tic(timer.c:81)
    at org.gccbridged.ecos.preproc__.ECOS_setup(preproc.c:577)
    at org.gccbridged.ecos.ECOS.ECOS_setup(Unknown Source)
    at ecos.RandomFeasible.main(RandomFeasible.java:31)

Thanks for help and all the best
Christian

messages.body_plain:
Hi Christian!
The compiler actually generates these "UnsatisfiedLinkExceptions" at compile-time when it can't find a function referenced by the source. In this case, it looks like it's a system function called "clock_gettime":
http://linux.die.net/man/3/clock_gettime

I've just committed a quick implementation for this function that should get you further:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/aeb8e5f145238b1c58123003c4f22b5a267f2f58

HTH,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Renjin not found Error
messages.body_plain:
Ah ok, this is in the context of an OSGI application.

To be honest, I am thoroughly confused by OSGI so I'm not sure I'm the best resource. (Anyone else out there have a better understanding? Recommend a good resource?)

A few observations though:

1. The NoClassDefFoundError means that Renjin is simply not on the classpath when this error occurred. So the issue lies somewhere in your project setup.

2. The page you linked to makes a good suggestion to help debug the problem. After you bundle your jar,  run:
unzip -l target/MyApp.jar | grep jar

You should see renjin-core.jar, renjin-script-engine.jar, etc in the bundle.

3. Some of Renjin's dependencies are packaged as OSGI dependencies (guava, for example), others are not. I honestly don't know if this will affect anything, but perhaps the Cytoscape team can tell you more.

4. There is an open issue to make Renjin a fully blessed OSGI bundle. Work on this is stalled because I just don't know enough about OSGI to put together a real test case. (Help and contributions in this area are most welcome)
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/121

Sorry I can't be of more help!

Alex

messages.subject: Re: After gcc-bridge compilation java implementation causes troubles with structs and/or throws runtime exception with UnsatisfiedLinkException
messages.subject_clean: After gcc-bridge compilation java implementation causes troubles with structs and/or throws runtime exception with UnsatisfiedLinkException
messages.body_plain:
Aha!
Looks like the C code is trying to get a pointer to the free() function. GCC-Bridge basically compiles free() to a no-op, so we need a new dummy method for which we can return a MethodHandle when needed. I've add this here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/9c1bee9a2938e6785a3aaab301d36d6a64b72c45

The same can be done for malloc if needed by creating a method that just returns a MallocThunk.

Alex

>
> 1. The NoClassDefFoundError means that Renjin is simply not on the classpath when this error occurred. So the issue lies somewhere in your project setup.
>
> 2. The page you linked to makes a good suggestion to help debug the problem. After you bundle your jar,  run:
> unzip -l target/MyApp.jar | grep jar
>
> You should see renjin-core.jar, renjin-script-engine.jar, etc in the bundle.
>
> 3. Some of Renjin's dependencies are packaged as OSGI dependencies (guava, for example), others are not. I honestly don't know if this will affect anything, but perhaps the Cytoscape team can tell you more.
>
> 4. There is an open issue to make Renjin a fully blessed OSGI bundle. Work on this is stalled because I just don't know enough about OSGI to put together a real test case. (Help and contributions in this area are most welcome)
> https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/121
>
> Sorry I can't be of more help!
>
> Alex

messages.body_snippet: Thanks for the pointer to the project set up. After searching some time in the cytoscape discussion group, I found that the error was that I had to update the maven-bundle-plugin from 2.3.7 to 3.0.1

messages.subject: Re: Renjin not found Error
messages.body_plain:
Glad to hear it!!

On Thu, Jun 23, 2016, 4:05 PM Rmdal <roosh...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the pointer to the project set up. After searching some time in the cytoscape discussion group, I found that the error was that I had to update the maven-bundle-plugin from 2.3.7 to 3.0.1
>
>

> >
> > Ah ok, this is in the context of an OSGI application.
> >
> > To be honest, I am thoroughly confused by OSGI so I'm not sure I'm the best resource. (Anyone else out there have a better understanding? Recommend a good resource?)
> >
> > A few observations though:
> >
> > 1. The NoClassDefFoundError means that Renjin is simply not on the classpath when this error occurred. So the issue lies somewhere in your project setup.
> >
> > 2. The page you linked to makes a good suggestion to help debug the problem. After you bundle your jar,  run:
> > unzip -l target/MyApp.jar | grep jar
> >
> > You should see renjin-core.jar, renjin-script-engine.jar, etc in the bundle.
> >
> > 3. Some of Renjin's dependencies are packaged as OSGI dependencies (guava, for example), others are not. I honestly don't know if this will affect anything, but perhaps the Cytoscape team can tell you more.
> >
> > 4. There is an open issue to make Renjin a fully blessed OSGI bundle. Work on this is stalled because I just don't know enough about OSGI to put together a real test case. (Help and contributions in this area are most welcome)
> > https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/121
> >
> > Sorry I can't be of more help!
> >
> > Alex
> >
> >

messages.subject: Re: renjin-dbi - H2 support
messages.body_plain:
Hi Erwan,
I believe that the tests for MySQL, Oracle, Postgres all rely on having a specific database set up on the build machine. Ideally we should have a Dockerfile or vagrant set up, but that's not the case right now so I believe these will fail.

For your new H2 module, it sounds like your test is failing:

library(hamcrest)
library(RH2)

test.driver <- function() {
con <- dbConnect(RH2(), url="jdbc:h2:file:/tmp/db", username="sa", password="")
renjinDBITest(con)
}

You can check target/renjin-test-reports/ to see the output from the failing test:
Executing test.driver... FAILED
ERROR: object of type 'closure' is not subsettable
  at structure()
  at JDBC()
  at RH2()
  at dbConnect()
  at test.driver()

It looks like the error is coming from this statement:
JDBC(JDBC$new(), "H2")

The expression JDBC$new() is meant to instantiate the Java JDBC driver class, which you properly imported in your NAMESPACE file:

importClass(org.h2.Driver)

If I change the statement above to

JDBC(Driver$new(), "H2")

Then your test passes.

HTH,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: RandomForest feedback
messages.body_plain:
Hi Erwan,
Unfortunately I haven't had the time yet to set up and run your benchmark. I'm doing some related work on performance this week so i'll try to take a look.

One thing that could help in the meantime would be to share some output from Renjin's (fledgling) profiler:

The big question for me about your example is whether the issue is with the C/Fortran code in randomForest that we compile to JVM bytecode, or whether the slowdown is occurring in interpreted R code.

If it's the former case, then we need to take a deep dive into GCC-Bridge and see what's going wrong and how we can improve the efficiency of the bytecode we're generating. If it's the latter, then there are many more possible villains. It could be that one or more primitive implementations is slower than GNU R, or perhaps something more general.

You can enable the profiler by including -Drenjin.profile=true as an argument to the JVM. The output might help point us in the right direction.

Best,
Alex

The only things I am aware of is a toy example in c https://github.com/bedatadriven/gcc-bridge-example and a real life library blas which is written in fortran: https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/tree/master/math/blas

You can easily try your c++ code buy just cloning renjin https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin make a mvn clean install. after that you simply make a maven folder structure where all your c++ sources go into src/main/cpp/ - use the pom from the blas link above as a starting point. then just do mvn clean install in your cpp maven project and see what happens. from my point of view gcc bridge is very early stage, while it has some proof  of concept a lot of things are not working yet. but this is the most promissing c/c++/fortan to jvm converter ever! the only alternative is nestedvm and it is very complicated to get the build chain sette up properly to compile to mips code. i have even tried to use mips debian linux on qemu but it ws still not easy.

cheers
chris

messages.subject: Re: renjin-dbi - H2 support
messages.body_plain:
Hi Erwan,
You have a few options:
1) You should be able to include org.renjin.cran:RH2 in any Java project after building to test.
2) You can write integration tests in Java or in R by adding test cases to src/test/java and src/test/R respectively
3) You can test interactively by running `mvn renjin:repl` from the H2 directory.
4) You can run `mvn install` on your project, which will copy the results to your ~/.m2/repository directory and then launch the renjin command line tool

Once you're ready, please submit a pull request and then it will get built and included in the Renjin repository so that it's available for everyone.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: After gcc-bridge compilation java implementation causes troubles with structs and/or throws runtime exception with UnsatisfiedLinkException
messages.subject_clean: After gcc-bridge compilation java implementation causes troubles with structs and/or throws runtime exception with UnsatisfiedLinkException
messages.body_plain:
I think this issue with structs/records requires some more thought.

Right now, the class names of structs are _not_ guaranteed to be stable across builds. Unlike function names, the names of types have no special meaning to GCC. They essentially disappear once the C is lowered to RTL and then machine code.

For this reason, it's not unusual to have different structs with the same name across several compilation units. GCC-Bridge's only concern at this point is to make sure the resulting Java classes have unique names. And more broadly speaking, the representation of records are subject to change as GCC-Bridge evolves. For example, we now compile structs who have homogenous fields (think struct point { double x; double y; }) to arrays rather than Java classes as it's more efficient and allows easy casting between pointers and different struct types.

For Renjin itself, there are however, a handful of structs like SEXP and MethodDef that we also need to be part of a stable API that makes interop between Java language code and C language code possible.

The solution we came up with here is to define <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/tools/gnur-runtime/src/main/java/org/renjin/gnur/api/MethodDef.java> the struct in Java, and then tell the compiler <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/ad219d404454cff0b415b5f78854acbd9eb64f67/tools/gnur-compiler/src/main/java/org/renjin/gnur/GnurSourcesCompiler.java#L184> to map structs with that name to this class.

The other thing we can consider is to just to make the autogenerated names of the records more stable across builds, for example, by sorting the record types first on a hash of their fields so that at least names will be stable across builds.

HTH,
Alex

I suppose you could also add the dependencies directly to RHS2, but I can see how you would want to avoid that if the dependencies are huge. The alternative would then indeed be to create a second module that depends on your RH2 module as well as the additional GIS dependencies.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Erwan,
For Renjin, we've tried to align the package/module system as closely as possible with existing build tools for the JVM. So you should be able to basically clone the RH2 module and change the dependencies in the pom.xml file.

I'm not sure that anything will need to be changed in the NAMESPACE file -- would this involve exposing more functions/methods to the R environment, or just ensuring that the GIS dependencies are on the classpath? In the latter case, you can simply leave the NAMESPACE file empty.

Best,
Alex
